text:
maria: Hey team — customer BrightMetrics is seeing a sudden spike in 429s and p95/p99 token latency from their dedicated pool eu-west-1-pool-7 starting ~2026-03-15T04:00Z. It lines up with another tenant on the same node launching a heavy batched workload.

maria: Symptoms: 429 RateLimitExceeded responses for short requests, p95 token latency jumped from ~80ms -> 800ms, p99 > 2s. Error rate ~6% for the tenant.

maria: Pool details: pool-id=eu-west-1-pool-7, node-ids=[node-31,node-32], MIG config on nodes: "7x 1g.5gb" slices on A100 (so many small MIG slices).

maria: Relevant logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T04:12:08Z ERROR 429 tenant=brightmetrics route=/v1/generate token_latency_ms=1200 request_id=abc123
2026-03-15T04:12:09Z WARN  queue_delay_ms=2500 tenant=brightmetrics
2026-03-15T04:12:10Z INFO  autoscale-check pool=eu-west-1-pool-7 active_slots=24 max_committed=24
```

maria: NV metrics while incident active (monitoring): GPU_SM_util=96-100%, GPU_mem_util=60-75%, L3_bandwidth_spikes=high, sm_efficiency_drop on slices colocated with heavy batch tenant.

maria: Repro steps I ran (on staging with smaller scale):
```
# simple concurrency test hitting the same model route
for i in `seq 1 100`; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"open-7b","input":"x"}' &\
  if (( i % 20 == 0 )); then wait; fi\
done
```
Observed 429s when concurrency ~>20 and when another workload batched with size=64 started on same node.

jess: Thanks Maria — can you paste the tenant_id and the exact node-id where brightmetrics is seeing errors? Also confirm whether the pool is configured with autoscale.max_committed == active_slots (looks like it's at cap).

maria: tenant_id=tenant_brightmetrics_998, node=node-31. Autoscale config: min=8, max_committed=24, burst_policy=disabled. autoscale logs show "no capacity to add due to committed cap".

autoscale-bot: [autoscale] 2026-03-15T04:12:15Z PolicyEval: pool=eu-west-1-pool-7 active=24 committed=24 can_scale=false reason=committed_capacity_reached

ryan: This looks like classic noisy-neighbor SM saturation on MIG slices. With many 1g slices you can still have shared physical SM contention and L3 cache thrashing if one tenant issues lots of large-batch matmuls. Need the following from Maria to triage:
- nvidia-smi dmon or NVML snapshot during spike (SM, mem, enc, dec)
- per-tenant qps and token-rate series for last 30m
- container-level GPU metrics (sm_util per MIG slice)

sam: If autoscale can't add more due to committed cap, short-term mitigations:
- bump committed reservation for that customer (if contract allows) to allow autoscale to add slots
- temporarily move brightmetrics to a node with fewer co-tenants / larger MIG slices (single-slice if possible)
- throttle the noisy tenant (if we can identify) via placement policy to reduce batch concurrency

leila: Longer-term config suggestions:
- prefer fewer larger MIG profiles for latency-sensitive customers (e.g., 2x 3g slices instead of 7x 1g), reduces SM cross-talk and L3 thrash
- add placement policy option `strict_isolation=true` for Dedicated pools so we don't co-locate high-batch tenants with low-latency tenants
- improve autoscale policy to consider SM utilization signals (not just slot counts) for scale triggers

maria: I captured a quick reproducer command to simulate the heavy-batcher we saw:
```
# simulate heavy batch client that pushes large matmuls
python3 - <<'PY'
import requests,threading
KEY="$KEY"
def req():
  requests.post('https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization':f'Bearer {KEY}'}, json={'model':'open-7b','input':'x'*2000,'batch_size':64})
threads=[threading.Thread(target=req) for _ in range(30)]
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
PY
```
This reliably increased SM util to >95% and caused 429s for colocated slices within ~60s.

ryan: Good reproducer, thanks. Next steps I'll need from infra: the NVML dump + perf counters (memory_bw, l3_bw, sm_eff) from node-31 during the window. Also please snapshot pod CPU/GPU cgroup stats and kube events (evictions, throttles).

jess: I've opened a support ticket and assigned to eng-runtime and infra: ticket #SUP-2026-0192. Action items:
- infra (sam) gather NVML/perf dmon from node-31 and attach to ticket
- eng-runtime (ryan/leila) evaluate MIG reconfiguration options and placement policy changes for pool
- support (maria) offer customer short-term migration to an isolated node or increase committed reservation

sam: I'll try a live migration for brightmetrics to node-45 (has 2x 3g slices and lower co-tenant load) — scheduling at 04:45Z. If migration not possible, will throttle the noisy tenant via placement override.

autoscale-bot: [autoscale] 2026-03-15T04:45:50Z ScaleEvent: pool=eu-west-1-pool-7 action=migrate tenant=tenant_brightmetrics_998 from=node-31 to=node-45 reason=manual_mitigation by=sam

maria: After migration to node-45 p95 dropped back to ~95ms and 429s dropped to near 0 within ~2m. Leaving this thread open for postmortem + config follow-ups.

jess: Thanks — we'll run a short postmortem and propose these changes: (1) autoscale policy: use SM util signal, (2) placement policy: strict isolation flag for latency SLAs, (3) guidance for sales/CS to recommend larger MIG slices for latency-critical customers.

ryan: I'll add a small repro job in infra-staging to simulate the heavy-batcher and validate detection heuristics (SM util >85% + queue_delay > 500ms) to trigger emergency scaling or placement eviction.

maria: Leaving notes for customer and scheduling a follow-up with BrightMetrics to discuss dedicated sizing. Thanks all :thumbsup:
